model.name: Tax Obligation / Assessment
model.purpose: Represent an authority-qualified tax obligation and its declarations, calculations, assessments, notices and time-qualified balances independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns obligation identity, tax and jurisdiction profile, liable-party and authority references, legal basis, taxable period and scope, return links, tax-base and calculation assertions, assessments, notices, due components, balance snapshots, adjustments, disputes and external payment or collection links. Taxpayer, law, source transaction, asset, payroll, return document, payment, audit case, debt and enforcement masters remain external.
in_scope: Obligation identity, taxpayer and authority references, tax classification, jurisdiction, legal basis, taxable event, period and scope
Return and source-evidence links, tax base, calculation origin, assessment, notice, due date and componentized balance
Amendment, relief, reassessment, limitation, dispute, audit, payment, collection, access, retention, interoperability and safe operations
out_of_scope: Taxpayer, authority, legal instrument, source transaction, asset, payroll, invoice, return document or payment master records
Audit, objection, appeal, debt collection, court case, enforcement or refund-payment master lifecycles
Universal tax calculation, automated legal interpretation, tax advice, assessment issuance or enforcement without competent authority

boundary_notes.distinction: The taxpayer remains an external party master; this model records obligation-specific liable-party capacity and registration references.
The return is an external taxpayer assertion and document; the obligation records its identity, filing evidence and declared totals.
A payment retains transaction identity; the obligation records allocation and a derived balance snapshot.
These are external proceedings with their own authority and lifecycle; the obligation records typed links and quantified effects.
A due or collectible amount can seed an external debt or enforcement process but is not itself that process.

functions.name: Register tax obligation
functions.description: Create authority-qualified obligation identity, tax profile, liable-party references and explicit potential-liability status.
preconditions: authority, identity namespace and tax profile validate
effects: obligation becomes resolvable without asserting final liability

functions.name: Bind legal basis and taxable scope
functions.description: Attach source-qualified law, period, place, taxable-event references, exemptions and allocation assertions.
preconditions: source versions, jurisdiction and effective interval validate
effects: potential scope becomes attributable and reviewable

functions.name: Ingest return assertion
functions.description: Link an external return or declaration and preserve filer assertion, receipt, acceptance and amendment chain.
preconditions: taxpayer, period, return version and source digest validate
effects: declared liability is recorded separately from assessment

functions.name: Assemble tax base calculation
functions.description: Build a source-linked calculation with components, rates, deductions, credits, rounding and origin.
preconditions: inputs, rule versions, currency and calculation origin validate
effects: calculation becomes reproducible without replacing source ledgers

functions.name: Record assessment decision
functions.description: Record a self-assessment, authority assessment, estimate or reassessment with competent authority and legal-effect semantics.
preconditions: competence, source, affected period and amount components validate
effects: assessed liability is established as a distinct assertion

functions.name: Notify and establish due balance
functions.description: Record notice evidence, legal-effect time, due date and a componentized payable and collectible balance snapshot.
preconditions: recipient, delivery, legal-effect rule, currency and dispute status validate
effects: notice and balance become queryable without treating them as payment

functions.name: Amend, correct, relieve or reassess
functions.description: Append a successor change with authority, reason, deltas, limitation and preserved predecessor.
preconditions: authority, deadline, affected components and predecessor head validate
effects: history remains immutable and current assertions are explicit

functions.name: Link audit, objection or appeal
functions.description: Connect external audit and dispute processes and record their effect on amounts and collection status.
preconditions: case identity, authority, affected assessment and suspension rule validate
effects: disputed and undisputed portions remain distinguishable

functions.name: Apply payment, credit or collection reference
functions.description: Reconcile an external payment, credit, refund, debt or enforcement reference into a new balance snapshot.
preconditions: external identity, currency, allocation and value date validate
effects: balance changes without importing or rewriting the external master

functions.name: Issue projection or retire obligation
functions.description: Create a purpose-bound exchange view or record closure, archive and retention without deleting cited history.
preconditions: access, freshness, finality, legal hold and retention validate
effects: consumer receives a traceable view or governed terminal state

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative master-system obligation identifier qualified by tax authority, jurisdiction and tax profile, never by taxpayer name, tax type, period, date or amount.
Keep potential, declared, assessed, payable, disputed, collectible and collected amounts as separate source-qualified assertions.
patch_rules: Extensions declare jurisdiction and tax profile, target finding, legal source, authority, classifier and exchange-profile versions and interoperability impact.
Changes to obligation identity, assessment authority, amount semantics, due or legal-effect rules, or access require a successor revision, migration map and preserved cited history.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, authority, law, period, amount components, assertion origin, time, access and provenance remain intact.
Every SAF-T, return-schema, LegalRuleML or sector projection pins versions and states transformed fields, omissions, code translations and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system obligation or assessment identifier qualified by tax authority and jurisdiction.
Governed globally resolvable obligation IRI bound to the authoritative system.
Dimension UUID or ULID when no external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate taxable-event, filing, receipt, assessment, notice, legal-effect, due, payment, observation and knowledge times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {obligation-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use taxpayer name, tax type, period, date, amount or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, authority, jurisdiction, tax and schema versions, legal source anchors, event and knowledge times, currency, access marking, quality and provenance.

policies: Only the competent tax authority or legally authorized filer may establish official assessment, filing or adjustment assertions.
Potential liability, declaration, assessment, notice, payable balance, disputed amount, collectible amount, payment and collection remain distinct.
Rates, bases, relief, limitation, appeal rights and collection effects are jurisdiction-specific source-qualified profiles, never universal agent defaults.
Agents may perform reversible clerical operations and propose calculations; legal interpretation, adverse assessment, disclosure, enforcement and write-off require accountable authority.

read: Resolve Dimension, authority, jurisdiction, tax profile, obligation head, event and knowledge time, access purpose and external masters.
create: Create obligation identity, parties, tax profile, legal basis and explicit unknowns before attaching returns, assessments, notices or balances.
update: Append return, calculation, assessment, notice, balance, amendment or process-link assertions with actor, authority, legal source, time and provenance; never overwrite cited history.
delete: Apply statutory retention, legal hold, dispute and records policy; prefer closure or tombstone and never cascade deletion to taxpayers, laws, returns, source records, payments, audits or cases.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of an authority-qualified tax obligation and assessment across OECD, United Nations, European Union, TADAT, OASIS, W3C and IETF primary materials, without universal tax calculation, legal interpretation, tax advice, assessment issuance or certified crosswalk claims.

checklist.notes: Authority-qualified obligation identity is separated from taxpayer, return, assessment, payment and collection masters.
Tax type, obligation class, jurisdiction and administration profiles are versioned.
Parties, legal basis, tax period, taxable scope, calculation, assessment, notice and balance assertions are first-class.
Return, source evidence, filing, notice, payment reference and audit evidence are covered.
Register, bind scope, ingest, calculate, assess, notify, amend, link, reconcile, project and retire operations are governed.
Returns, ledgers, invoices, payroll, assets, payments, audits, disputes and enforcement retain external master identity.
Potential, declared, assessed, notified, due, disputed, adjusted, satisfied, closed and archived states preserve history.
Taxpayer, authority, law, event, source record, return, payment and proceeding links are typed.
Tax period, filing, assessment, notice, legal-effect, due, payment, observation and knowledge times remain distinct.
Residence, source, place of supply, situs and jurisdiction are source-qualified references.
Calculations, decisions, notices, adjustments and balance snapshots retain source and responsible-agent provenance.
Taxpayer, law, source record, return, payment, audit, dispute, debt and enforcement masters remain separate.
Identity, authority, period, source, calculation, currency, notice, balance and stale-head checks are explicit.
Taxpayer, authority, auditor, dispute, exchange and analytical views are purpose-bound.
Returns, assessments, notices, amendments, disputes, allocations and legal holds are preserved.
SAF-T, return-schema, LegalRuleML, PROV and time projections are versioned and loss-aware.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later tax-domain review is required before canonical promotion.
Jurisdiction-specific tax types, rates, bases, deductions, credits, relief, limitation, filing, assessment, appeal and collection profiles require specialist review.
No approved model-relation rows were supplied; composition targets remain reviewable draft references.
Certified SAF-T, return-schema, LegalRuleML and tax-system crosswalks and conformance fixtures remain future work.
conflicts: Potential, declared, assessed, payable, disputed, collectible and collected amounts can legitimately differ.
Taxpayer calculations, authority calculations, estimates, amendments and reassessments may coexist and supersede only within a declared assertion chain.
Filing, assessment issuance, notice, legal effect, due, payment and knowledge can occur at different times and under different rules.
regional_assumptions: The VAT Directive is an EU profile and is not a universal tax ontology.
The UN Model Convention is a treaty model and applies only through adopted agreements and domestic law.
TADAT evaluates tax-administration performance and does not itself establish taxpayer liability.
adversarial_checks: Reject an obligation identified solely by taxpayer name, tax type, period, date, amount or document digest.
Reject a return or taxpayer calculation represented as an authority assessment without a competent decision.
Reject a current balance that merges disputed, suspended, collectible, paid and written-off amounts without source-qualified components.
Reject replacement of an assessment or return without immutable amendment or reassessment lineage.
Reject an agent action that interprets tax law, issues an adverse assessment, discloses sensitive data or destroys cited history without accountable authority.

boundaryDecision.status: accepted as an authority-qualified obligation aggregate with separately identified assertions and balance snapshots
boundaryDecision.rationale: The aggregate owns obligation identity, obligation-specific party and legal bindings, declared and assessed assertions, notice and balance views. Taxpayers, laws, source records, return documents, payments, audits, disputes, debts and enforcement processes preserve their own master identity and lifecycle.

decisions.concept: Obligation versus taxpayer, return, payment and debt
decisions.rationale: The obligation is one authority-qualified aggregate; parties, declarations, transactions and collection processes remain referenced masters.

decisions.disposition: accepted as external parties with obligation-specific roles
decisions.rationale: Identity, registration and organizational records are external, while liable-party capacity, representation and competence are time-qualified bindings.
A taxable event may imply potential scope, a return records a taxpayer assertion, and an assessment records a competent authority or self-assessment assertion.

decisions.concept: Self-assessment, authority calculation, estimate and reassessment
decisions.disposition: accepted as source-qualified calculation and decision variants
decisions.rationale: Origin, method, assumptions, evidence, authority and successor lineage must remain explicit so competing calculations are not silently merged.
Principal, credit, interest, penalty, payable, disputed, suspended, collectible, paid and written-off amounts can legitimately differ.
Tax period, event, filing, receipt, assessment, notice, legal effect, due, payment, observation and knowledge time cannot be collapsed into one date.
Corrections, relief, amended returns and reassessments change current assertions but never erase cited predecessor evidence or decisions.
These processes have separate authority, identities and lifecycles; the obligation records typed links and quantified effects only.
SAF-T, return schemas, LegalRuleML, PROV and temporal standards address different concerns and cannot replace authoritative obligation state.
Agents may maintain records and propose validations or calculations but cannot interpret governing tax law, issue adverse assessments, give tax advice or enforce without accountable authority.

model.name: Tax Return / Filing
model.purpose: Represent a versioned tax declaration package, its filing attempts and authority acknowledgements so agents can prepare, validate, sign, transmit, amend and reconcile tax-reporting context without confusing submission with receipt, acceptance, assessment, payment, refund, compliance or finality.
model.scope_statement: Owns return and revision identities; original, amended, corrected, superseding, supplemental, final, nil and information-return classes; taxpayer, tax account, registration, obligation, tax type, period and jurisdiction bindings; preparer, signer, representative, transmitter, software and tax-authority roles; form sections, lines, schedules, supplementary pages, elections, claims, disclosures, explanations and attachments; reported facts, amounts, currencies, units, bases, deductions, credits and declared-tax calculations; source-document and external-record evidence bindings; form, schema, taxonomy, code-set and business-rule versions; structural, completeness, cross-field and business validation; attestation, signature, mandate, consent and digest evidence; filing attempts, channels, endpoints, envelopes, payloads, postmarks, idempotency, retries and replacements; receipt confirmations, acknowledgements, rejection codes and accepted-for-processing responses; independent lifecycle axes and deadlines; non-destructive amendment, correction, supersession and withdrawal lineage; payment, refund, offset, penalty, interest, assessment, audit, inquiry, appeal, collection and records references; provenance, quality, clocks, tax secrecy, privacy, access, retention and loss-aware projections. External taxpayer, tax account, law, calculation-engine, invoice, payroll, payment, refund, assessment, audit, dispute, enforcement and generic document masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Return and revision identity, obligation, taxpayer, jurisdiction, form structure, facts, evidence, calculations, validation, signature, filing attempts and acknowledgements
Lifecycle, deadlines, amendments, downstream references, clocks, provenance, privacy, access, retention, validation and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Taxpayer, Tax Account, Tax Law, Calculation Engine, Invoice, Payroll, Payment, Refund, Assessment, Audit, Dispute, Enforcement or generic Records masters
Treating prepared as signed, submitted as received, schema-valid as accepted, accepted-for-processing as assessed, declared tax as authority liability, or return amount as payment or refund
Autonomous legal attestation, signature, filing, payment, validation override, protected-data disclosure or record destruction

boundary_notes.distinction: The unified registry supplies WM-POL-011 as a provisional parent signal only. Tax policy and administration remain external and no settled containment edge exists.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Taxpayer, tax account, obligation and tax law
boundary_notes.distinction: The return binds external parties, accounts, obligations and versioned legal profiles; it does not own their identity or lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Declaration, filing attempt, acknowledgement and assessment
boundary_notes.distinction: A return revision declares facts, an attempt transmits a payload, an acknowledgement reports a channel or authority outcome, and an assessment is a separate authority determination.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Declared values, liability, payment and refund
boundary_notes.distinction: Reported or calculated values do not prove an assessed liability, settled payment, offset, refund entitlement or refund execution.
Each tax, reporting, currency, signature, privacy or schema source covers a scoped profile; every mapping is version-pinned and loss-declaring.

functions.name: Initialize return
functions.description: Governed operation to initialize return without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
preconditions: namespace, taxpayer authority, obligation, period, jurisdiction and form version are resolved
effects: creates a draft return only and does not create taxpayer, account, law, assessment, payment or records masters

functions.name: Bind taxpayer and obligation
functions.description: Governed operation to bind taxpayer and obligation without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
preconditions: identity, authority, tax type, period, jurisdiction and filing mandate are known
effects: binds external masters without copying their lifecycle or secret credentials

functions.name: Assemble declaration package
functions.description: Governed operation to assemble declaration package without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
inputs: sections, schedules, facts, elections and attachments
preconditions: required sections, line identities, classifications and attachment rules are pinned
effects: assembles the declaration without asserting signature, submission, receipt or acceptance

functions.name: Ingest source evidence
functions.description: Governed operation to ingest source evidence without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
inputs: source documents and external record references
preconditions: source identity, authority, period, freshness, access and correction lineage are known
effects: records evidence and never treats it as a declared fact, assessed value or payment by itself

functions.name: Derive declared values
functions.description: Governed operation to derive declared values without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
outputs: basis, deduction, credit and declared-tax assertions plus derivation trace
preconditions: formula, rate, threshold, code, currency, period, source and rule versions are pinned
effects: creates declared values that do not prove authority assessment, liability, payment or refund

functions.name: Validate return
functions.description: Governed operation to validate return without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
preconditions: structural, completeness, type, cross-field and business controls are resolvable
effects: records pass, fail, warning or waiver evidence without silently changing the declaration

functions.name: Attest and sign
functions.description: Governed operation to attest and sign without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
preconditions: signer identity, consent, mandate, declaration text, digest and signature time are confirmed
effects: adds a signature event and never implies transmission, receipt, acceptance or assessment

functions.name: Submit and record acknowledgement
functions.description: Governed operation to submit and record acknowledgement without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
outputs: filing attempt and correlated authority response
preconditions: delegated filing authority, deadline, payload digest, channel, schema and endpoint versions are valid
effects: records independent submitted, received, rejected and accepted-for-processing assertions

functions.name: Amend, supersede and reconcile
functions.description: Governed operation to amend, supersede and reconcile without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
outputs: successor return, lineage and reconciliation assertions
preconditions: original remains immutable and authority, period, impact, deadlines and downstream obligations are known
effects: preserves history and never infers reassessment, payment recovery, refund or dispute resolution

functions.name: Validate, project, retain and audit
functions.description: Governed operation to validate, project, retain and audit without autonomous legal attestation, filing, payment, protected-data disclosure or destruction.
outputs: validation report, minimum view, loss declaration, retention result or audit event
preconditions: schema, digest, authority, privacy, legal-hold, clock and conformance checks pass
effects: never exposes unnecessary tax data or cascades deletion into taxpayer, account, assessment, payment, dispute or records masters

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize a return by authoritative tax authority or taxpayer-system identifier, taxpayer, tax type, tax period, jurisdiction, form or report type and revision head, never by filename, amount, submission time or digest alone.
Canonicalize every filing attempt and authority response separately from the declaration revision; keep declared values, assessments, payments, refunds and disputes distinct.
patch_rules: Extensions declare return class, jurisdiction, form, section, fact, calculation, evidence, filing channel, response and interoperability effects.
Signed, submitted or accepted revisions are immutable; amendment, correction, supersession and withdrawal create linked successors with reason, authority and downstream impact.
Never silently change taxpayer, obligation, tax period, jurisdiction, form, schema, currency, reported amount, signature, filing state, authority response, privacy marking or external reference.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when return and revision identity, taxpayer, obligation, period, jurisdiction, form, values, states, clocks, authority, access and provenance survive.
Every projection pins schema, form, taxonomy, code-set, currency and jurisdiction versions and declares loss in calculation, filing, lifecycle, privacy and authority semantics.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for a tax return, filing, acknowledgement, assessment, payment or records object, qualified by namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable return, filing-attempt or artifact IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish tax-period boundary, due, preparation, validation, signature, submission, electronic-postmark, receipt, rejection, acceptance-for-processing, assessment, payment, refund, correction, observation, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, return and revision IDs, actor, purpose, source, form, schema, taxonomy, rule and policy versions, amount type, currency, unit, precision, event and knowledge times, confidentiality, retention and provenance.

policies: This model owns the governed return declaration package, filing attempts and authority acknowledgements, not taxpayer, tax account, law, calculation engine, invoice, payroll, payment, refund, assessment, audit, dispute, enforcement or generic document masters.
Prepared, validated, signed, submitted, received, accepted-for-processing, assessed, paid, refunded, disputed and final remain separate assertions.
Jurisdiction, taxpayer class, tax type, form, filing channel, calculation, evidence, retention and privacy rules are versioned profiles rather than universal defaults.
Agents cannot autonomously make a legal attestation, sign, file, pay, waive validation, disclose protected tax data or destroy records without explicit delegated authority.

read: Resolve return, revisions, obligation, parties, sections, facts, evidence, rules, signatures, attempts, responses, amendments, downstream references, access and projection loss.
create: Bind taxpayer, return class, obligation, tax period, jurisdiction, form, schema and initial unknown lifecycle states before adding declared facts.
update: Append successor facts, validations, signatures, filing attempts, acknowledgements, amendments, corrections and reconciliation assertions with reason, authority, source, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply tax secrecy, privacy, audit, legal-hold and Dimension retention policy; tombstone only the catalogue view and never cascade deletion to external masters.

access.default_rule: Deny taxpayer identifiers, returns, reported facts, income, deductions, credits, bank data, signatures, assessments, payments, disputes and authority responses unless purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared taxpayer, preparer, legal, tax-authority, payment, audit, security or incident access must cite authority, scope, purpose and time limit and be logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, return and revision IDs, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected assertions, source revision and outcome without duplicating protected values, credentials or destinations.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
WM-POL-011 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-032 edge.
Income, corporate, partnership, payroll, VAT, excise, customs, property, estate, gift, information-return, international, consolidated-group and sector profiles need separate validation.

Taxpayer identity, tax accounts, substantive tax law, calculation engines, source transactions, assessments, payments, refunds, audits, disputes, enforcement, privacy and retention remain adopting-Dimension profiles.
Every IRS, HMRC, EU, OECD, CRA, XBRL, ISO, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL, XML Signature and OpenAPI mapping needs exact release pins and conformance tests.
conflicts: Return declaration, filing attempt, acknowledgement, assessment, payment, refund, dispute and enforcement action are related but not equivalent identities.
Original, amended, corrected, superseding, supplemental, final, nil and information returns require explicit classes and lineage.
Reported amount, calculated declared tax, authority-assessed liability, payment, offset and refund are distinct axes.
Prepared, validated, signed, submitted, received, schema-valid, accepted-for-processing, assessed, paid, refunded, disputed and final are independent states.
regional_assumptions: Obligation, taxpayer classification, return form, evidence, calculation, signature, filing, assessment, correction, retention and tax secrecy depend on jurisdiction and tax type.
IRS, HMRC, EU, OECD and CRA sources are scoped profiles and not universal tax law.
adversarial_checks: Reject a return record that lacks separate return-revision and filing-attempt identities.
Reject a return that absorbs taxpayer, tax account, law, invoice, payroll, payment, refund, assessment, audit, dispute, enforcement or records masters.
Reject an amount without amount type, currency, unit, rule version, source, period, precision and provenance.
Reject submission as proof of receipt, schema validity, acceptance, assessment, payment, refund, compliance or finality.
Reject an amendment that destructively overwrites the filed predecessor.
Reject autonomous signature, filing, payment, validation waiver, protected-data disclosure or deletion without delegated authority.

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

It owns the versioned declaration package, filing attempts and authority acknowledgements, while taxpayers, tax accounts, substantive law, assessments, payments, refunds, audits, disputes and records remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: The model owns declaration revisions, filing attempts and acknowledgements, not every upstream tax fact or downstream authority and payment lifecycle.
The unified registry supplies WM-POL-011 as a parent hint but the frozen relation ledger has no settled WM-ECO-032 edge, so it grants no containment or cascade authority.

decisions.concept: Return revision, filing attempt and acknowledgement
decisions.rationale: A revision declares facts, an attempt transmits a particular payload and an acknowledgement records a correlated channel or authority response.

decisions.concept: Prepared, signed, submitted, received, valid, accepted, assessed and paid
decisions.rationale: No preparation, signature, transport, validation or processing state silently proves a later authority determination or settlement.

decisions.concept: Reported value, declared tax, assessed liability, payment and refund
decisions.rationale: Every value preserves type, currency, rule version, period, source and derivation and cannot prove a separate authority or transaction record.

decisions.concept: Original, amended, corrected, superseding, supplemental, final, nil and information return
decisions.rationale: Each class has distinct legal effect, validation, lineage and downstream processing and cannot be inferred from filename or sequence alone.
The original filed revision remains immutable while a successor states change set, reason, authority and downstream impact.

decisions.concept: Taxpayer, account, law, assessment, payment, refund, audit, dispute and enforcement
decisions.rationale: The return may bind or project data to these models but does not absorb their identity, authority or lifecycle.

decisions.concept: Jurisdiction, tax type, form, schema and filing channel
decisions.rationale: Official sources define scoped regimes and releases; no form, deadline, calculation, signature or acceptance rule is universal.

decisions.concept: Tax secrecy, privacy, access and segregation
decisions.rationale: Taxpayer identity, return facts, income, deductions, bank data, signatures, assessments and disputes require purpose-bound least privilege and auditable exceptions.
XML, XBRL, JSON, YAML, files, APIs and databases are projections of the same model and must pin profiles and declare loss.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-032 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.

Slash-boundary hold: this aggregate covers return declaration revisions, filing attempts and acknowledgements, while upstream tax facts and downstream authority or transaction lifecycles remain external.
Relation hold: WM-POL-011 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-032 edge.
Identity hold: taxpayer, tax account, return revision, filing attempt, acknowledgement, assessment, payment, refund, dispute, enforcement and records objects remain distinct.
Lifecycle hold: prepared, validated, signed, submitted, received, schema-valid, accepted-for-processing, assessed, paid, refunded, disputed and final states do not prove one another.
Value hold: reported amount, calculated declared tax, authority-assessed liability, payment, offset and refund remain separately sourced and currency qualified.
Amendment hold: amendments, corrections, supersessions and withdrawals preserve predecessors and declare downstream obligations rather than overwriting history.
Privacy hold: taxpayer identifiers, reported facts, income, deductions, bank data, signatures, assessments and disputes require tax secrecy, purpose limitation and minimum disclosure.
Source-access hold: the prior OECD legacy resource URL failed direct retrieval and was replaced by its current official resource-centre URL verified through official indexed content.
Profile hold: income, corporate, partnership, payroll, VAT, excise, customs, property, estate, gift, information-return, international and consolidated-group uses need separate profiles.

Interoperability hold: every tax, reporting, currency, signature, temporal, provenance, quality, privacy, policy and API projection needs exact release pins, conformance evidence and loss declarations.
Review hold: tax, legal, filing, accounting, privacy, security, records and independent external review are outstanding.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

model.name: Tax Filing / Assessment Process
model.purpose: Represent a governed tax filing and assessment case so agents can connect return preparation, validation, declaration, submission, authority determination, settlement references and dispute without treating any transport or workflow state as proof of legal finality or payment.
model.scope_statement: Owns one filing-and-assessment case identity for a defined taxpayer reference, tax type, jurisdiction and period; return composition and source lineage; calculation and validation results; declaration, submission and acknowledgement links; self-assessed and authority-determined positions; adjustments, notice and liability references; settlement, penalty and dispute links; and correction lineage. Taxpayer, registration, account, obligation, law, form, source document, ledger, evidence, payment, refund, penalty, audit, examination, dispute, collection, enforcement, adjudication, provenance, access audit and record masters remain external.
in_scope: Case identity and tax scope; return, schedule and attachment composition; source lineage, calculations, validations, declaration, submission and acknowledgement
Self-assessment, authority assessment and adjustment context; notice and liability references; payment, refund, penalty and dispute links; correction, privacy, retention and loss-aware projections
out_of_scope: Creating or changing taxpayer, tax account, obligation, law, form, source record, payment, refund, penalty, examination, dispute, collection, enforcement or court masters
Equating receipt with acceptance, acceptance with processing, self-assessment with authority assessment, payment with full satisfaction, or notice with finality
Providing tax advice, signing or filing without authority, moving money, deciding an assessment or appeal, or destructively handling tax evidence

boundary_notes.neighbor: Taxpayer, registration, tax account, obligation and law models
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters retain authoritative identity and lifecycle. The case stores typed, versioned references and a bounded filing scope without rewriting them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Return, schedule, attachment, declaration, submission and acknowledgement
boundary_notes.distinction: Each record has independent identity, authority, status and time. A technical receipt is not a legal acceptance or assessment.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Audit, examination, assessment, collection, enforcement and adjudication
boundary_notes.distinction: Specialist processes own selection, evidence gathering, decisions and enforcement. This aggregate records links, notices, amounts, reasons, deadlines and status intake.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Payment, refund, interest and penalty models
boundary_notes.distinction: Authoritative financial systems own money movement and balances. The case stores typed allocation and status references without inferring universal satisfaction.
Specialist models own proceedings and outcomes. This aggregate retains the disputed items, grounds, evidence links, deadlines, stays and result references.

boundary_notes.neighbor: MeF, HMRC VAT API, XBRL, UBL, XML Signature and PROV
boundary_notes.distinction: These are versioned jurisdictional or technical projections with different scopes. No mapping is assumed lossless or universally applicable.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize each case and constituent by authoritative master-system identifier, tax administration and record kind; never by taxpayer, period, form, date, amount or status alone.
Keep return, schedule, attachment, declaration, submission, acknowledgement, assessment notice, liability, payment, refund, penalty and dispute independently identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare jurisdiction, tax type, filing season, form, schema, business-rule, signature, privacy, retention and interoperability effects.
Released returns, submissions, acknowledgements, assessments, notices, allocations and dispute records are immutable; corrections create linked successors.
Never silently change taxpayer, obligation, period, source values, calculation, declaration, signature, status, amount, reason, deadline, authority or provenance.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, tax scope, record kind, source, authority, status, time, evidence and provenance survive.
Every projection pins jurisdiction, tax type, filing season, form, schema, business rules, signature profile and code-list versions and declares information loss.

identity_priority: Authoritative tax-administration or master-system identifier for each case, return, submission, acknowledgement, assessment, liability, payment, refund, penalty, dispute or notice, qualified by administration and record kind.

Dimension UUID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish tax period, source effective, due, signed, submitted, postmarked, received, acknowledged, accepted, processed, assessed, served, paid, appealed, recorded, ingested and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, tax scope, form and rule versions, actor, authority, event and knowledge times, status, access marking and provenance.

policies: The aggregate does not own Taxpayer, Registration, Tax Account, Tax Obligation, Law, Form, Source Document, Ledger, Evidence, Payment, Refund, Penalty, Audit, Examination, Dispute, Collection, Enforcement, Adjudication, Provenance, Access Audit or Record masters.
Technical validation, business validation, transmission receipt, filing acceptance, processing, self-assessment, authority assessment, payment and dispute outcome remain separate assertions.
Receipt does not prove validity or acceptance; acceptance does not prove assessment finality, payment, absence of penalties or dispute resolution.

Agents cannot give tax advice, sign declarations, file returns, initiate payments, change authority decisions, waive appeal rights, disclose tax data or dispose records outside explicit delegated authority.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
No relation-ledger edge is registered for WM-ACT-052, so links to taxpayer, obligation, document, evidence, payment, audit, assessment, dispute and records models remain candidate boundary notes.
Income, corporate, payroll, withholding, consumption, property, customs and other taxes require jurisdiction and tax-type profiles.
OECD sources are comparative or advisory; IRS and HMRC are jurisdiction-specific; XBRL, UBL and XML Signature require implementation-profile and conformance validation.
conflicts: A return, submission, acknowledgement, assessment notice, liability, payment, refund, penalty and dispute are not interchangeable.
Structural validation, business-rule validation, transmission receipt, filing acceptance, processing and legal acceptance are separate outcomes.
Self-assessed and authority-determined values must retain their sources, and payment does not prove satisfaction of every obligation.
regional_assumptions: Tax liability, filing, assessment, penalties, interest, dispute, finality, retention and disclosure depend on jurisdiction, tax type, period and facts.
IRS sources are United States profiles, HMRC sources are United Kingdom profiles, and the VAT Directive and GDPR are European Union profiles.
OECD guidance is not domestic law; forms, schemas, business rules, code lists, signature methods and administrative procedures must be versioned.
adversarial_checks: Reject a case or constituent without stable identity, taxpayer and obligation references, tax type, jurisdiction, period, authority, status and lineage head.
Reject a filing claim that equates transmission, receipt, acceptance, processing, assessment or payment.
Reject an assessment that overwrites the return position or lacks issuer authority, provision, calculation, reason, notice, effective time and review rights.
Reject an amendment or replacement that loses original return, submission receipt, governing versions or predecessor-successor lineage.
Reject autonomous tax advice, declaration signature, filing, payment, authority decision, appeal waiver, protected disclosure or disposition outside explicit authority.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The subject composes multiple independently identifiable returns, schedules, declarations, submissions, acknowledgements, assessment notices, liabilities, allocations and disputes over one governed case. Aggregate is more accurate than event. The frozen record_plane world-model and catalogue entry_kind standalone-mm are separate axes from this subject-schema decision.

decisions.rationale: The aggregate owns only the bounded filing-and-assessment case. Taxpayer, registration, account, obligation, law, form and authority records remain external and are referenced with versions and roles.
Return, schedules and attachments preserve source records, data cut, computation, currency, units, rounding and reconciliation without absorbing ledger or evidence masters.
Schema, code-list, business-rule, signature, transmission, receipt, filing acceptance and processing outcomes remain independently attributable and timed.
Taxpayer positions and authority-determined values retain separate sources. Adjustments require provision, calculation, reason, notice, effective time and review-right context.
Payment, refund, penalty, interest and adjudication records remain external. The case owns typed allocations, disputed-item context, deadlines, stays and outcome references.

No relation-ledger edge is registered. Plausible links to taxpayer, obligation, document, evidence, payment, audit, assessment, dispute and records models remain candidate boundary notes and create no cascade behavior.

OECD material is comparative or advisory, IRS and HMRC are jurisdiction-specific, and EU instruments require current transposition and procedural context. No source is generalized into universal tax law.
MeF, HMRC VAT API, XBRL, UBL, XML Signature and PROV cover different filing, reporting, document, signature and provenance surfaces. Every mapping must pin version, scope and information loss.

One Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 research attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex audited the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts. Confidence remains medium and assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 research attempt for WM-ACT-052 each timed out after 120 seconds. No external research result was admitted.
Relationship-completeness hold: no relation-ledger edge is registered for taxpayer, obligation, document, evidence, payment, audit, assessment, dispute or records models.
Jurisdiction and tax-type hold: filing, assessment, liability, penalties, interest, dispute, finality, retention and disclosure require current jurisdiction, tax type, period and authority profiles.
Source-scope hold: OECD sources are comparative or advisory; IRS, HMRC and EU sources have bounded legal or administrative scope and cannot be generalized silently.

Interoperability hold: MeF, HMRC VAT API, XBRL, UBL, XML Signature and PROV projections require release-pinned mappings, scope constraints, licensing review where applicable, loss declarations and validation.
Tax-status hold: receipt, acceptance, processing, assessment, payment, refund, penalty and dispute resolution remain separate assertions and no published state proves legal finality or satisfaction.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

Create current jurisdiction and tax-type profiles for income, corporate, payroll, withholding, VAT or GST, property, customs and other taxes.

model.name: Legal Instrument / Norm
model.purpose: Represent an authority-backed legal instrument and the norms expressed by its addressable source fragments, independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns legal-work, expression, manifestation, source, provision and norm linkage; instrument class; authority and legal-basis references; structure and citations; authenticity and provenance; deontic assertions; lifecycle, temporal applicability, interpretation, access and projections. Organizations, lawmaking procedures, cases, enforcement events, affected parties, places and generic document storage remain external masters.
in_scope: Legal work, expression, manifestation, item, authoritative source, provision and norm identity
Authority, class, structure, citation, normative meaning, lifecycle, time, applicability, conflict and provenance
Authentication, consolidation, controlled disclosure, retention, interoperability and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Issuing organization, legislative or administrative procedure and generic document repository masters
Court or arbitration case, enforcement event, affected person, asset and place masters
Automated legal advice, universally binding interpretation or substantive law common to every jurisdiction

boundary_notes.distinction: Authorities are external organizations referenced in a specific legal capacity; the legal instrument owns neither their identity nor governance.
The process produces adoption and publication evidence; the instrument aggregate preserves outputs and lifecycle assertions but not the workflow master.
A case may interpret, invalidate or apply an instrument, but its parties, procedure, evidence and decision lifecycle remain a separate model.
A policy or rule may lack legal-source authority; this aggregate requires explicit legal-source, jurisdiction and competent-authority bindings.
Files and records are manifestations or evidence items; they do not replace authority-qualified legal-work identity or normative semantics.

functions.name: Register legal work

effects: the work becomes resolvable without collapsing its expressions

functions.name: Add expression or manifestation

preconditions: work and derivation resolve

functions.name: Authenticate authoritative source

preconditions: publisher role and evidence are known

functions.name: Address provision and citation

preconditions: source versions and numbering history resolve
effects: provisions stay citable across rendition and renumbering

functions.name: Bind norm to source
functions.description: Attach a structured or formal norm to exact source fragments with author, method and confidence.
preconditions: source fragments and expression version resolve
effects: formal semantics remain attributable and contestable

functions.name: Record legal lifecycle event
functions.description: Append adoption, publication, commencement, suspension, repeal, expiry or correction evidence.
preconditions: competence, affected scope and times validate
effects: state changes without overwriting prior assertions

functions.name: Construct consolidated view
functions.description: Apply cited modifications to create a dated non-authoritative or authority-qualified consolidated expression.
preconditions: all applied sources and unresolved conflicts are explicit
effects: the view remains distinct from original acts

preconditions: versions, jurisdiction and authority scope resolve
