model.name: Jurisdiction
model.purpose: Describe, in a storage- and interface-neutral way, the bounded competence of an authority: which authority-holder may act, over what territory, persons, subject matter and period, on what legal basis, and how that competence relates to, yields to or is excluded by other competences.
model.scope_statement: A Jurisdiction record binds an identified authority-holder to a delimited competence and records the evidence for that delimitation. It covers identity and coding of jurisdictions and their subdivisions; the conferring instrument and category of competence; the four scope axes (territorial, personal, material, temporal); the declared type of power (prescriptive, adjudicative, enforcement) as a classification only; relations between jurisdictions (hierarchy, concurrency, exclusivity, delegation); immunities, reservations and derogations that narrow scope; lifecycle change including succession and cession; provenance, contestation and validation; and interoperability with external territorial and legal identifier schemes. It does not author geometry, does not hold legal instruments, does not decide a concrete case, and does not evaluate, execute, enforce or audit anything at runtime.
in_scope: Identity, naming and versioned records for jurisdictions and jurisdictional subdivisions, including supranational, State, sub-State and specialised tribunal scopes
Alignment to external territorial code lists (ISO 3166-1/-2 as normatively referenced by other standards, UN M49, EU Countries and territories NAL, NUTS) without asserting conformance
Authority-holder binding by reference and the conferring or constituting instrument cited as legal basis
Category of competence and exclusivity (exclusive, shared, supporting/coordinating) and the principle of conferral
Territorial scope by reference, including land territory, internal waters, territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone, continental shelf and superjacent airspace
Personal scope and connecting factors (domicile, habitual residence, nationality, seat, place of conduct, place of effect, targeting)
Material or subject-matter scope, including declared subject-matter competence catalogues
Temporal scope: entry into force, applicability window, non-retroactivity and jurisdiction ratione temporis
Declared classification of power type as prescriptive, adjudicative or enforcement competence
Inter-jurisdictional relations: hierarchy and supremacy, subsidiarity, concurrency, priority and lis pendens references
Immunities, privileges, reservations, opt-outs, derogations and carve-outs that narrow declared scope
Forum-selection and recognition bindings recorded as references to the governing instrument
Lifecycle of the jurisdiction record: establishment, extension, reduction, transfer, cession, merger, split, suspension, termination and State succession
Provenance, official-publication attestation, contested or overlapping claims, and validation status with currency
out_of_scope: Authoring or storing boundary geometry, coordinate reference systems or topology; these belong to the parent place and administrative-unit spatial model
Holding the text, consolidation, FRBR expressions or in-force computation of legal instruments; these belong to the legislation model addressed by ELI and Akoma Ntoso
Deciding the competent forum, the applicable law or the outcome of a concrete dispute; this model produces advisory candidate sets only
Runtime policy evaluation, decision execution, enforcement action and enforcement outcomes; these are owned by a referenced policy-decision and enforcement runtime model
Audit-trail semantics, audit record schemas and audit retention execution; the model emits provenance about its own records only and never owns another model's audit trail
Court dockets, case files, judgments and case-law citation graphs, which belong to the case-law identification model addressed by ECLI
Organisational structure, appointments, budgets and staffing of the authority-holder, held in the public-authority organisation model
Legal-entity master data such as LEI reference data, ownership structures and registration-authority records, mastered by GLEIF and Local Operating Units
Statistical territorial classification for reporting purposes as an authority claim; NUTS units are statistical and are aligned to, not treated as, jurisdictions
Natural-person nationality, citizenship or residence registries, and postal address formats
Tax rate schedules, treaty-benefit computation and customs tariff calculation

boundary_notes.neighbor: Parent place and administrative-unit spatial model (WM-PLC-004; INSPIRE Administrative Units theme)
boundary_notes.distinction: The spatial model owns AdministrativeUnit and AdministrativeBoundary features, their geometry, national levels and boundary editing lifecycle. Jurisdiction carries only a resolvable reference to those features plus the competence semantics attached to them, and never re-authors or re-versions geometry locally.

NUTS levels exist to enable collection and dissemination of European statistics and are built from administrative units subject to population thresholds and a triennial amendment cadence. A NUTS unit is therefore an alignment target for reporting, not evidence that an authority holds decision-making power over that area.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Legislation and legal-instrument model (ELI, Akoma Ntoso Naming Convention)
boundary_notes.distinction: ELI and the Akoma Ntoso FRBR Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item stack own instrument identity, versioning and publication. Jurisdiction cites an instrument as the legal basis for a competence; it must not mirror expression-level versioning, consolidation or in-force computation of that instrument.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Applicable-law / conflict-of-laws model (Rome I, Regulation (EC) No 593/2008)
boundary_notes.distinction: Rome I governs which law applies to a contractual obligation, including party choice, default connecting rules, overriding mandatory provisions and the public-policy exception. Brussels Ia governs which court has jurisdiction. Choice of law and choice of forum are separate determinations and this model owns only the forum-scope side, by reference.

ECLI identifies individual judgments through country code, court code, year and ordinal number. Jurisdiction may align to the ECLI court code as an identifier for an adjudicative authority, but judgments, dockets and citation metadata are not modelled here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Legal-entity registry model (ISO 17442 / GLEIF Global LEI Index)
boundary_notes.distinction: The LEI record masters an entity's legal jurisdiction and registration authority as entity reference data. Jurisdiction consumes those values as connecting-factor inputs by reference and never becomes a second master for entity reference data.

This model supplies scope facts and advisory candidate sets. Evaluation of a rule against a case, issuance of a decision, enforcement action against a party outside the territory, and the audit trail of those acts are wholly owned by the runtime model. Enforcement jurisdiction is recorded here only as a declared classification, never as an executed capability.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Territorial code maintenance agencies (ISO 3166 series, UN M49, EU Countries and territories NAL)
boundary_notes.distinction: Code assignment, retirement and re-use rules belong to the maintaining agency. UNSD explicitly states that grouping assignments are for statistical convenience and imply no position on political affiliation or legal status. Alignment entries here are assertions with a match strength, not conformance claims.

UNCLOS fixes zone breadths and the content of coastal-State rights per zone. A maritime jurisdiction record specialises the generic Jurisdiction entity with zone type, baseline reference and deposited-coordinate reference; it does not redefine zone entitlements, delimitation methodology or dispute settlement machinery.

functions.name: Register a jurisdiction record
functions.description: Create a new jurisdiction record binding an authority-holder to a delimited competence, with at least one conferring instrument reference and an identifier assigned by the identity priority rule.
inputs: scope declarations across the four axes
preconditions: authority-holder resolvable in the referenced organisation or court register
at least one conferring instrument citable by a governed legal identifier
identity priority applied and the tier recorded
effects: creates a draft record that asserts no legal validity of its own
records the attestation and observation instant for every asserted element

functions.name: Align to an external territorial code
functions.description: Record an alignment assertion between a jurisdiction record and an externally maintained territorial code, with match strength, pinned scheme version and any published neutrality caveat.
outputs: caveat carry-over where the scheme publishes one
preconditions: the code scheme has a named maintenance agency and a retrievable release
no conformance is claimed unless explicit evidence is supplied
effects: adds a dated alignment assertion
never mutates the external code or the local identifier

functions.name: Declare spatial extent by reference
functions.description: Bind a jurisdiction to administrative-unit features or maritime and aerial zone declarations without storing geometry locally.
inputs: administrative unit or boundary feature references
baseline reference and deposited coordinate reference
outputs: zone rights enumeration where the extent is a functional zone
preconditions: geometry is authored and versioned in the referenced spatial model
for maritime zones, the zone type and its outer limit rest on a citable declaration
effects: binds references and zone semantics only
leaves geometry authorship, topology and boundary lifecycle entirely with the spatial model

functions.name: Resolve candidate jurisdictions
functions.description: Return an ordered advisory set of jurisdictions whose recorded scope matches supplied connecting factors, subject matter and reference instant, each with its basis of connection.
inputs: connecting factors such as situs, domicile, habitual residence, nationality, place of conduct, place of effect and targeting indicators
outputs: ordered candidate set with basis of connection and confidence
contested-result flag with competing claim references
preconditions: reference instant supplied in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
scope records evaluated only in states valid at that instant
effects: produces advisory context only
does not select the competent forum, determine applicable law, decide a case or trigger any enforcement

functions.name: Assess overlap and priority
functions.description: Classify the relation between two or more jurisdictions over a shared scope as exclusive, concurrent, hierarchical or disputed, and cite the recorded priority rule.
preconditions: each record is in a state valid at the reference instant
competing claims, if any, are already recorded as separate assertions
effects: records a dated, attributable assessment with provenance
never silently merges or suppresses a competing claim

functions.name: Record a scope change
functions.description: Apply a controlled change event to a jurisdiction record, closing the prior version's validity interval and opening a new one, with the effecting instrument cited.
outputs: closed prior version with retained content
preconditions: instrument reference resolvable through a governed legal identifier
effective instant and observation instant supplied as distinct fields
effects: supersedes rather than overwrites the prior version
retains the prior version under the retention class for the record type

functions.name: Record succession, cession or dissolution
functions.description: Link predecessor and successor jurisdictions when competence is transferred, merged, split or extinguished, recording the share of scope passing to each successor.
outputs: tombstone entry where the predecessor is extinguished
preconditions: the succession basis is citable
the identifier continuity rule has been applied and its outcome recorded
effects: preserves historical resolvability of the predecessor identifier
marks the predecessor obsolete rather than deleting or reassigning it

functions.name: Register an exception or immunity
functions.description: Record an immunity, privilege, reservation, declaration, opt-out or derogation that narrows declared scope for a beneficiary class over a validity window.
outputs: exception entry scoped to beneficiary and window
link to the depositary declaration record
preconditions: a declaration, reservation or instrument evidences the exception
the enumerated defeating exceptions, if any, are recorded alongside
effects: narrows the declared scope for the named class in recorded form
does not grant, refuse or waive immunity in any concrete matter

functions.name: Crosswalk to an external identifier scheme
functions.description: Add or update a mapping between a jurisdiction record and the jurisdiction token used by ELI, ECLI, LEX URN, Akoma Ntoso, a territorial code list or a legal-entity register.
preconditions: the target scheme has a published registry and a documented governance or registrar rule
token syntax constraints of the target scheme are satisfied
effects: adds a versioned interoperability mapping
records conflicts explicitly instead of resolving them silently

functions.name: Validate a jurisdiction record
functions.description: Run the pinned validation profile over a record version, producing a rule-by-rule report and setting validation status and currency.
outputs: last verified instant and next due instant
preconditions: profile version pinned and immutable for the run
every asserted element carries at least one attestation
effects: blocks promotion from draft to published on blocking failures
sets a staleness clock that triggers reverification

functions.name: Apply retention and disposition
functions.description: Determine and record the disposition outcome for a superseded, withdrawn or terminated record, leaving a tombstone and delegating physical destruction to the owning policy.
outputs: disposition outcome of retain, tombstone, transfer or destroy
tombstone entry preserving the identifier and successor link
confirmation evidence request to the executing actor
preconditions: a superseding version exists or a termination event is recorded
the owning records policy reference resolves to a named executing actor
effects: never hard-deletes a published jurisdiction identifier and never permits reassignment
records the decision locally while the physical disposition is executed by the adopting Dimension under its own policy

composition.purpose: Jurisdiction records are navigated beneath the parent place model, which owns place identity, administrative-unit features and boundary geometry. This model contributes competence semantics attached to those places and never re-authors place identity or geometry.

composition.target: Administrative unit and boundary spatial model (INSPIRE Administrative Units theme)
composition.purpose: Carry resolvable references to AdministrativeUnit and AdministrativeBoundary features, the national administrative level and spatial anomalies, plus jurisdiction-specific parameters such as which competence attaches to which unit. Geometry authorship, topology, boundary editing and their lifecycle remain wholly in the spatial model.

composition.target: Territorial code registries (ISO 3166-1 and ISO 3166-2 as normatively referenced, UN M49, EU Countries and territories NAL)
composition.purpose: Assert dated alignments with a match strength and a pinned scheme version, carrying forward any published neutrality caveat. Code assignment, retirement and reuse policy stay with the maintenance agencies and no conformance is claimed without evidence.

composition.target: Legislation and legal-instrument model (ELI, Akoma Ntoso, LEX URN)
composition.purpose: Cite conferring, amending and terminating instruments through governed legal identifiers together with a pinpoint provision and a relation type. Instrument text, FRBR expression versioning, consolidation and in-force computation remain owned by the legislation model.

Bind the authority-holder by reference with a role qualifier and continuity links. Organisational structure, appointments, internal competence allocation, dockets and operational activity are not modelled here.

Align adjudicative jurisdiction records to the ECLI country and court codes so that decisions can be attributed to a competence record. Judgment records, ordinal assignment and citation graphs remain in the case-law model.

composition.target: Legal-entity registry model (ISO 17442 / GLEIF Global LEI Index)
composition.purpose: Consume an entity's legal jurisdiction and registration authority as connecting-factor inputs for personal-scope evaluation. Entity reference data remains mastered by GLEIF and its Local Operating Units and is never duplicated as local master data.

composition.target: Applicable-law and conflict-of-laws model (Rome I and equivalents)
composition.purpose: Keep choice of forum separate from choice of law by referencing, not reproducing, the applicable-law determination, including overriding mandatory provisions and the public-policy exception. Determining the governing law of a relationship is owned entirely by that model.

composition.target: Policy-decision, enforcement and audit runtime model
composition.purpose: Supply jurisdiction scope facts and advisory candidate sets as inputs. Rule evaluation, decision issuance, enforcement action, representative-based service mechanisms and the audit trail of all of these are owned by the runtime model and are never modelled, executed or logged here.

composition.target: Statistical territorial classification model (NUTS, Regulation (EC) No 1059/2003)
composition.purpose: Map jurisdictions to statistical territorial units for reporting, while recording that NUTS units are statistical constructs subject to population thresholds and a triennial amendment cadence and therefore carry no authority claim of their own.

Specialise the Jurisdiction entity for maritime and aerial zones by adding zone type, baseline reference, outer limit and deposited-coordinate reference. Generic identity, authority binding, lifecycle, provenance and conflict machinery are inherited and are not restated in the specialisation.

Reuse a shared contract for effective-time versus observation-time intervals, supersession and version identity, so that this model records only jurisdiction-specific interval semantics such as entry into force and applicability windows.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a competent public or legal authority, or an accountable steward acting on published sources, as owner of every jurisdiction record it publishes; unowned records may exist only in draft state.
The owner package must declare, per record class, which retention class applies and which actor executes physical disposition, since disposition execution lies outside this model's boundary.

The owner package must pin the versions of every external scheme it aligns to (territorial code lists, ELI, ECLI, LEX URN, NUTS) and must subscribe to their change notifications so that alignments can be invalidated when a registrar retires a token.
The owner package must publish its neutrality posture, carrying forward the caveats of any source that disclaims a position on the legal status of territories or the delimitation of frontiers.
The owner package must declare which policy-decision or enforcement runtime consumes its outputs, and must record that evaluation, enforcement and audit are executed there.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one stable namespace per adopting Dimension for locally minted jurisdiction identifiers, kept strictly separate from the namespaces of external registrars. Never mint a local identifier in a shape that could be mistaken for an ISO 3166, M49, ELI, ECLI or LEX URN token. Local subdivision hierarchies should mirror the parent-child structure of the record graph rather than encoding hierarchy in the identifier string, so that reorganisation does not force a rename that external schemes forbid.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-pol-015 (model WM-POL-015) is the canonical registration for this model and records its parent WM-PLC-004.

External registrar links must be recorded per alignment: the maintenance agency for each territorial code list, the ELI implementation register of the publishing authority, the ECLI national coordinator, and the LEX URN Jurisdictional Registrar where one is designated.

Composition targets that are not yet registered Vercy models must be recorded as named placeholders with their intended relation type so that the ownership contract is auditable before the sibling model exists.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form is the semantic record graph, not any serialisation: JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, a Git tree, an MCP resource and a document collection are equivalent projections and none is normative.

Order-insensitive collections (alignment entries, crosswalk entries, competing claims, exception entries) are canonicalised by sorting on their member identifiers before digesting, so that projection ordering cannot change a digest.
All instants are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds present and an explicit numeric offset or Z; no locale-dependent or offset-less form is canonical.
Identifiers are canonicalised case-sensitively as issued by their registrar; the model never normalises the case or punctuation of an external token.
patch_rules: Substantive changes to a competence create a new record version through record-scope-change; they are never applied as in-place edits to a published version.

A patch must carry the effecting instrument reference, the effective instant and the observation instant; a patch lacking an instrument reference may only alter attestation, alignment or crosswalk metadata, not scope.
Corrections of transcription error are recorded as errata against the same version with their own provenance, distinguishing correction of the record from change of the underlying competence.
Deleting an alignment or crosswalk entry is expressed as closing its validity interval, never as removal, so that historical resolution remains reproducible.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new optional data element, code-list term, alignment scheme or question is a minor change; removing or narrowing an element, retiring a code-list term, or tightening a cardinality is a breaking change.
Jurisdiction identifiers are permanently stable: they are never renamed, never reassigned and only ever marked obsolete with a successor link, following the LEX URN rule for jurisdiction codes.
A change to the meaning of a typology term requires a new term and deprecation of the old one; terms are never redefined in place.
Consumers must tolerate multi-valued and contested results; a scheme change that would force a single answer where the sources disagree is breaking.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the competent public or legal authority that constitutes or registers the jurisdiction — for example the national official register or gazette reference for the constituting instrument, the treaty depositary notification reference, the ECLI court code for an adjudicative body, or the statutory subdivision code issued by the national coding authority.

Governed global identifier or IRI from a maintained public registry — for example the EU Countries and territories NAL URI, an ELI URI for the conferring instrument, a LEX URN jurisdiction token, or an ISO 3166-1/-2 code as normatively referenced by Akoma Ntoso and urn:lex.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension in its own namespace, used only when neither of the tiers above yields a stable identifier, and always recorded together with the tier marker and the reason no higher tier applied.
A date, a name, a boundary geometry, a NUTS code or any statistical grouping code is never an identifier for a jurisdiction; NUTS and M49 codes may be carried only as alignments.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time strings that include seconds and an explicit numeric UTC offset or the literal Z; offset-less, date-only or locale-formatted values are rejected at validation. Event time and observation time are separate mandatory fields wherever they can differ: the effective instant records when a jurisdictional change took legal effect according to its instrument, while the observation or ingestion instant records when this model retrieved or recorded that fact. Where an instrument states only a date, the effective instant is recorded as a date-typed element with the governing time zone named explicitly rather than silently coerced to midnight UTC.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — the code alignment table, subject-matter competence catalogue, deposited coordinate records, depositary declaration records, official publication attestations, validation reports, the identifier crosswalk map and the tombstone register — are named as artifact identifier plus a monotonically increasing semantic version or run instant, never by overwriting a prior name. Each release pins the versions of every external scheme it depends on, is immutable once published, and links to the release it supersedes; the AGENTS.md bootstrap descriptor is the sole non-serial artifact and is replaced wholesale on version change.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact release carries a content digest and the retrieval instants and digests of the external sources it depends on, so that an agent can detect upstream drift. Attestation and tombstone registers are append-only. A digest mismatch against a pinned source sets the affected records to a stale state and blocks their promotion, but never rewrites the historical release; integrity of externally held instruments and geometry is verified by reference only, since those artifacts are owned by the legislation and spatial models.

policies: Alignment, not conformance: citing an external standard records a mapping with a match strength and pinned version. Conformance to ISO 3166, ELI, ECLI, Akoma Ntoso, LEX URN or INSPIRE is asserted only where explicit conformance evidence is recorded, and conflicts between schemes are preserved as conflict records rather than resolved editorially.

Neutrality on contested status: where authorities assert incompatible competence, all claims are held side by side with their asserting authority, instrument and instant. The model does not adjudicate, rank by political preference, or suppress a claim, and it carries forward source caveats disclaiming any position on legal status or delimitation of frontiers.

Advisory only: outputs are context for a decision-maker. The model never determines the competent forum for a concrete matter, never selects the applicable law, and never evaluates, executes, enforces or audits anything; those operations belong to the referenced conflict-of-laws and policy-decision runtime models.

Reference over replication: geometry, instrument text, entity reference data, judgments and audit trails are referenced through resolvable identifiers and are never copied into this model, even when copying would be convenient for offline use.
Evidence before publication: no record may leave draft state without at least one attestation naming an official publication or register, a retrieval instant and an authority tier.

read: Published jurisdiction records, their alignments, crosswalks, exceptions and provenance are readable by default at bundle, layer, finding and artifact scope.
Reads that supply a reference instant return the record version valid at that instant; reads without one return the current version and must state that fact in the response.
A read that matches competing claims must return all of them together with the contested-result flag; returning a single claim without disclosure is a contract violation.
Draft, embargoed and restricted records are readable only by roles holding the corresponding grant, and every such read requires a recorded justification.
create: Creation requires an authority-holder reference, at least one conferring instrument reference and an identifier resolved through the identity priority rule with its tier recorded.
New records are created in draft state; they carry no assertion of legal validity until validation passes and a steward promotes them.
Creating an alignment or crosswalk entry requires the pinned version of the external scheme and an explicit match or equivalence strength.
Creating a record for a contested scope requires the competing claims to be recorded as separate attributed assertions in the same transaction.
update: Scope changes are applied only through record-scope-change, which closes the prior version and opens a new one with distinct effective and observation instants.
Metadata-only updates to attestation, alignment or crosswalk entries do not create a new scope version but do create a new provenance entry.
No update may rename or reassign a jurisdiction identifier; an identifier may only be marked obsolete with a successor link.
An update that would resolve a recorded conflict without new attested evidence is rejected; conflicts are closed only by evidence, not by editorial preference.
delete: Hard deletion of a published jurisdiction record is prohibited. Withdrawal produces a tombstone that permanently preserves the identifier, the obsolescence instant, the successor link where one exists and an explicit reuse-prohibition assertion, so that historical citations in ELI, ECLI, LEX URN and Akoma Ntoso references continue to resolve.

Superseded versions are retained under the retention class assigned to the record type and are required for reconstructing the competence in force at any past instant; removal of a superseded version is an exception requiring a named approving role, a recorded reason and an approval instant.
Unpublished drafts that never entered published state may be removed outright, provided any attestation they created is retained in the append-only attestation register.

Execution of physical destruction, media sanitisation and any legally mandated erasure is outside this model's boundary: it is owned and executed by the adopting Dimension's records-management policy named in disposition-owner-ref, and where a referenced model holds the underlying material — the legislation model for instruments, the spatial model for geometry, the entity registry for entity data and the runtime model for audit trails — deletion there is owned by that model. This model records only the disposition decision, its trigger and the confirmation evidence returned by the executing actor.
Removal of an external alignment or crosswalk is expressed by closing its validity interval; the entry itself is never erased, because a past resolution must remain reproducible.

roles.name: Jurisdiction steward
responsibilities: Owns a defined set of jurisdiction records and their promotion from draft to published state
Ensures every asserted element carries an attestation with a retrieval instant and authority tier
Approves scope-change records and confirms the identifier continuity decision for each change
Maintains the neutrality posture when contested claims are recorded

roles.name: Legal source verifier
responsibilities: Verifies conferring and amending instrument citations against official publications and registers
Assigns and reviews authority tiers and primary or secondary markers for each source
Runs reverification against the staleness threshold and records the last verified instant
Raises errata where a record diverges from its cited source

roles.name: Spatial and boundary liaison
responsibilities: Maintains resolvable references into the administrative-unit and boundary spatial model and rejects any local geometry authoring
Records maritime and aerial zone types, baselines and deposited coordinate references
Coordinates with the parent place model when unit references are retired, split or merged
Flags enclave, exclave, condominium and shared-administration anomalies for steward review

roles.name: Interoperability registrar
responsibilities: Maintains crosswalks to ELI, ECLI, LEX URN, Akoma Ntoso, territorial code lists and legal-entity registers
Pins external scheme versions and monitors registrar change notices for retired or obsoleted tokens
Records conflicts between schemes rather than resolving them and escalates them to the steward
Enforces the prohibition on renaming or reassigning jurisdiction identifiers

roles.name: Access and retention officer
responsibilities: Applies the open-by-default access posture and approves every documented exception with a reason and review instant
Assigns retention classes and confirms that a named actor and policy own physical disposition outside this model
Maintains the append-only tombstone register and verifies that no retired identifier is reused
Confirms that no personal data about identified natural persons enters jurisdiction records

access.default_rule: Jurisdiction records describe publicly constituted authority and are open by default at every scope, because their evidentiary basis is official publications, treaty depositary records and public registers that are themselves published.
exceptions: Draft records and pre-publication scope changes are restricted until promoted, to avoid circulating an unattested competence claim as if it were in force.

Deposited coordinate records and boundary references may be restricted where the source authority itself embargoes them, and the embargo is carried forward with its source reference rather than re-decided locally.

Records describing a live contested claim may be access-flagged where publication would misrepresent a pending proceeding; the restriction applies to presentation, never to the underlying attested claims, which remain retained in full.
Internal conflict records and escalation notes are restricted to the steward and registrar roles until the conflict is closed by evidence.
Any restriction requires a named approving role, a recorded reason and a scheduled review instant; restrictions do not renew silently.
audit_requirements: Every access to a restricted or draft record must be evidenced with the accessing actor, the justification, the scope accessed and an RFC 3339 instant with seconds and offset.

The audit trail that stores this evidence is owned and operated by the adopting Dimension's audit system or the referenced runtime model; this model defines the required evidence fields but does not own audit-record schemas, audit retention or audit querying.
Grants and revocations of access are themselves recorded as provenance entries against the affected scope so that the access posture at any past instant can be reconstructed.
Restriction exceptions must be reviewed at their scheduled review instant, and an expired unreviewed restriction is reported as a validation failure.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and confirm that Name, Type, Registry ID and Model ID identify this model and version.
Read the Specification URL to load the bundle, layer, finding and question structure together with the scope statement, out-of-scope list and boundary notes before assuming any capability.
Read the Storage type URL to learn the projection in use (document store, graph, repository tree or service resource) and to confirm that the projection is not treated as semantics.
Read the Interface URL to learn how to query records at a reference instant, how contested and multi-valued results are returned, and which operations are refused.

Read the Processes URL to learn the registration, change, validation, retention and escalation procedures and which actors own operations that lie outside this model, in particular evaluation, enforcement, deletion execution and audit.

If any bootstrap target is unreachable, operate in read-only advisory mode against cached published records, state the degraded mode to the caller, and do not create, promote or dispose of any record.

coverage.claim: Reviewable-draft coverage for Jurisdiction as a bounded competence: identity and territorial coding, authority-holder and conferral, the four scope axes with declared power type, inter-jurisdictional relations and exceptions, lifecycle with provenance and contestation, and identifier interoperability — 6 bundles, 13 layers, 28 findings, 113 questions, 10 artifacts and 11 functions, with every layer resting on at least one tier-1 primary source. Coverage is EU- and UN-instrument-weighted and audited by one provider only; it is not complete for any national legal system, and non-State legal orders, arbitral competence, cross-border data-access regimes, State-succession instruments and outer space, Antarctic and deep-seabed regimes remain declared or newly identified omissions.

checklist.notes: jurisdiction-record-identity sets a three-tier priority headed by the authoritative master-system identifier; the LEX URN prohibition on renaming and obsolete-only retirement supplies primary support for permanent identifier stability, and NUTS and M49 codes are explicitly excluded as identifiers.

scope-change-succession-and-dissolution defines a controlled change-type set, record states and predecessor/successor continuity, grounded in the NUTS amendment cadence, ELI versioned publication and the treatment of State succession; identifier continuity is decided per change.

Hierarchy and deference, concurrency with priority rules, and forum-selection and recognition are separated into distinct findings grounded in Brussels Ia exclusive heads and lis pendens, Rome Statute complementarity, TFEU competence categories and the HCCH 2005 Convention.

temporal-applicability-window separates entry into force, applicability start and end, and retroactivity from record observation time; Rome Statute Article 11 with its Article 12(3) declaration supplies the primary case for reachable-conduct instants distinct from entry into force.
source-attestation-and-provenance requires per-assertion publication citation, retrieval instant, authority tier, digest and a derived-versus-attested marker; attestations are append-only.

authority-holder-binding carries the holder by reference only, and eleven composition links plus nine boundary notes assign geometry, instruments, entity data, judgments, applicable law, evaluation, enforcement and audit to their owning models.

validation-conformance-and-currency defines a pinned profile, blocking versus advisory severities, an explicit alignment-not-conformance default, and a staleness threshold that triggers reverification; the validation report is a serial immutable artifact.

Open-by-default posture across all four scopes with five narrow, reviewable exceptions; required access-evidence fields are specified while audit-record schemas and retention are explicitly assigned to the adopting Dimension or runtime model.

crud.delete prohibits hard deletion of published identifiers, mandates tombstones with reuse prohibition, retains superseded versions for reconstruction, and names disposition-owner-ref plus the adopting Dimension's records policy as the owner of physical destruction; per-model deletion of instruments, geometry, entity data and audit trails stays with those models.

external-identifier-crosswalk and jurisdiction-token-in-legal-identifiers map to ELI, ECLI, LEX URN, Akoma Ntoso, territorial code lists and LEI jurisdiction data, with equivalence strength, pinned scheme versions, conflict records and registrar-driven invalidation.

Land extent is reference-only into the INSPIRE-aligned spatial model; maritime and aerial zones are modelled as functional partial competences with zone type, baseline, outer limit and deposited-coordinate evidence per UNCLOS Parts II and V.

Competence category and exclusivity follow the TFEU taxonomy including the principle of conferral and pre-emption; delegation, devolution, sub-delegation limits and consensual bases are recorded with revocability.
Immunity with waiver and enumerated defeating exceptions, reservations, declarations, opt-outs and derogations are one scoped overlay finding, evidenced by depositary-lodged declaration records.

Jurisdiction kind is a governed code list artifact with per-term citation and deprecation; power type is recorded as prescriptive, adjudicative or enforcement classification only, with an explicit non-ownership pointer to the runtime model.

contested-claim-and-dispute-recording holds parallel attributed claims with a mandatory neutrality caveat drawn from the UNSD disclaimer, and the consumer contract forbids silent single-answer resolution.
Quantified elements are limited to zone outer limits, competence thresholds and staleness durations, each with units and a source; no scoring or ranking of jurisdictions is introduced.
Personal data about identified natural persons is excluded by design with an explicit assertion; personal-scope modelling operates on person classes and attachment criteria, not on individuals.

Restriction of embargoed deposits and drafts is handled through access exceptions with named approvers and review instants; no security-control implementation is claimed, since enforcement belongs to the runtime model.

Eleven functions cover registration, alignment, spatial binding, resolution, overlap assessment, change, succession, exception registration, crosswalking, validation and disposition, each with preconditions and non-ownership effects.
Attestation tiers, digests, derived-assertion flags, conformance-claim flags and currency instants together make each assertion falsifiable against a named source.

known_omissions: ISO 3166-1 and ISO 3166-2 could not be fetched directly: iso.org returned HTTP 403 on every attempt. The standard is therefore cited indirectly through instruments that normatively reference it (Akoma Ntoso Naming Convention, urn:lex) and through UNSD and the EU Countries NAL. Any structural claim resting solely on ISO wording should be treated as unverified until the ISO Online Browsing Platform is consulted.

The International Law Commission's 2006 annex on extraterritorial jurisdiction (A/61/10) could not be parsed; the prescriptive/adjudicative/enforcement trichotomy is therefore supported here by the operative structure of Brussels Ia, GDPR Article 3 and the UN Convention on Jurisdictional Immunities rather than by a doctrinal source. The power-type classification is marked as declared classification only and should be re-grounded if a retrievable authoritative statement of the trichotomy is obtained.

Religious, customary, indigenous and non-State legal orders are not separately modelled. The typology can express them as jurisdiction kinds, but no primary source in this set governs their identity, coding or conferral, so treating them as first-class here would be unsupported structure.

Arbitral tribunal competence, investor-State dispute settlement and the New York Convention regime are out of the source set; the consensual-basis element can carry an arbitration reference but the model asserts no structure for arbitral seat, kompetenz-kompetenz or award enforcement.

Cyberspace-specific and platform-jurisdiction questions (data localisation, jurisdiction over cloud-held evidence, cross-border production orders) are represented only through generic connecting factors; no instrument governing cross-border data access is cited.
Outer space, Antarctic Treaty area and deep seabed Area regimes are not modelled, although each is a genuine non-territorial competence regime; UNCLOS Parts XI and following were not consulted.
No source in this set defines a normative confidence scale, so confidence values on candidate sets and alignments are locally defined and are not comparable across adopting Dimensions.
Machine-verifiable conformance evidence for ELI, ECLI or Akoma Ntoso is not specified here; the model records only whether conformance is claimed and what evidence would be required.
conflicts: Territorial coverage of ISO 3166, UN M49 and the EU Countries and territories NAL is not identical: each includes entries the others omit or classify differently, and each maintains its own retirement policy. Alignments are therefore recorded per scheme with a match strength, and cross-scheme disagreement is preserved as a conflict record.

UNSD states that groupings are for statistical convenience and imply no position on political affiliation or legal status, while a jurisdiction record is precisely a claim about legal authority. The model resolves this by never inferring competence from a code-list membership and by carrying the UNSD caveat forward.

NUTS defines an administrative unit as an area with an authority holding decision-making power, yet NUTS levels themselves are statistical aggregations subject to population thresholds. Treating a NUTS unit as a jurisdiction is a category error the model blocks by classing NUTS as an ALIGN target only.

GDPR Article 3 asserts prescriptive reach over controllers with no EU establishment, while enforcement jurisdiction is territorially constrained. The model records prescriptive and enforcement scope separately and requires the asymmetry to be stated rather than smoothed.

Brussels Ia exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24 and party autonomy under Article 25 can point to different forums, and the HCCH 2005 Convention adds its own obligations on chosen and non-chosen courts with enumerated refusal grounds. The model records both bindings with their instruments and does not compute a winner.

Rome Statute complementarity means a competence can exist yet be inadmissible in a concrete case. The model separates existence of competence from admissibility, and admissibility determination is left to the adjudicating body.

The urn:lex requirement that jurisdiction codes are never renamed can conflict with national practice of reusing subdivision codes after reorganisation. The model follows the stricter urn:lex rule and forbids reuse locally, which may diverge from a national coding authority's own behaviour.

Immunity under the 2004 UN Convention operates as an exception to an otherwise existing jurisdiction, not as its absence; systems that model immunity as a scope reduction will produce different answers from systems that model it as an overlay. This model uses the overlay reading and states it explicitly.
regional_assumptions: The competence-category taxonomy (exclusive, shared, coordinating, supporting) and the principle of conferral are drawn from EU treaty law. They generalise reasonably to federal systems but are not universal; unitary and common-law systems may allocate competence by convention or judicial doctrine rather than by an enumerated list.

Brussels Ia, Rome I, ELI, ECLI and NUTS are EU instruments. Their structural lessons are used as evidence that particular distinctions exist and are operationally necessary, not as evidence that any specific rule applies outside the EU.

The 2004 UN Convention on Jurisdictional Immunities is not universally in force; several States apply national immunity statutes or customary law with materially different exceptions. Immunity entries must therefore cite the instrument actually relied on in the recording jurisdiction.
The HCCH 2005 Choice of Court Convention binds only its Contracting States; forum-designation entries must record the applicable regime rather than assuming the Convention applies.

Maritime zone entitlements assume UNCLOS as the reference frame; States not party to UNCLOS, and areas subject to pending delimitation, require the applicable bilateral or customary basis to be cited instead.

The open-by-default access posture assumes a legal system in which constituting instruments, registers and treaty depositary records are publicly published. Where they are not, the adopting Dimension must set a more restrictive default and record why.
adversarial_checks: Does any finding own a target model's operations? Checked every bundle, layer, finding and function against the composition rationales: power-type-classification and scope-resolution-procedure both carry explicit non-ownership pointers and are inline-only precisely so that no artifact could be mistaken for an enforcement or decision record; access audit requirements name required evidence fields but assign audit schemas, retention and querying to the adopting Dimension or runtime model; crud.delete records only the disposition decision and names the external executing actor.

Is any structure attractive but unsupported? A generic 'jurisdictional legitimacy' or 'sovereignty score' layer was rejected because no source in the set defines a normative measure, and any such structure would breach the neutrality policy. A separate 'enforcement action' layer was rejected for the same reason and reduced to a classification code with a limitation note.

Does the model duplicate a sibling? Boundary notes and composition links keep geometry with the spatial model, instrument text and versioning with the legislation model, judgments with the case-law model, entity reference data with GLEIF, applicable-law determination with the conflict-of-laws model, and evaluation, enforcement and audit with the runtime model. Land extent, legal basis, authority holder and forum designation are all inline reference-only findings for exactly this reason.

Is the exclusive-artifact rule satisfied everywhere? Ten findings declare artifacts with inline_only_rationale set to null; eighteen declare an empty artifacts array with a substantive rationale that explains why the context is reference or classification data. No finding populates both.

Would a counterexample break the structure? Tested against functional partial competence (UNCLOS EEZ: competence over enumerated activities only, coexisting with other States' freedoms), against competence without territory (an international tribunal reaching conduct by nationality link), against competence over conduct outside the territory (GDPR targeting), against competence created by private agreement (HCCH choice of court), and against competence that exists but yields (Rome Statute complementarity, Brussels Ia lis pendens). Each is expressible without adding structure, which is why plenary-or-functional, connecting-factor and deference elements exist.

Can the identity rule survive reorganisation? A jurisdiction that is split, merged or renamed keeps its identifier, gains an obsolescence marker where extinguished and a successor link with scope share; the urn:lex prohibition on renaming is enforced locally even where a national coding authority reuses codes, and this divergence is recorded as a known conflict rather than hidden.

Is anything claimed as conformance without evidence? No. The conformance-claim flag defaults to alignment, ISO 3166 is flagged as indirectly cited because iso.org was unreachable, and the prescriptive/adjudicative/enforcement trichotomy is marked as declared classification pending a retrievable doctrinal source.

Does the model force a single answer where sources disagree? No. Competing claims are returned together with a contested-result flag, the read contract makes suppressing a claim a violation, and closing a conflict requires new attested evidence rather than editorial preference.

providerPolicy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must not be conflated. On the record plane the frozen registry value standalone-mm says only that vr.wm-pol-015 is registered as a free-standing meta-model record with empty contains_ids and a single parent WM-PLC-004; it classifies the registration, not the subject, and is not a member of the subject-model enum. On the subject plane the most defensible schema kind is entity, and the declared value is accepted. The decisive test is identity independence: the jurisdiction identifier is permanently stable, never renamed or reassigned, survives reorganisation, renaming or abolition of the authority-holder (q-holder-continuity), survives extension, reduction, cession, merger and split (q-change-identifier), and on extinction is retired by obsolescence marker plus successor link rather than deleted. 'relationship' was seriously considered because the purpose binds a holder to a competence, but a reified relationship loses identity when an endpoint changes, which this model expressly forbids. 'aggregate' was considered because the record roots dependent collections (alignments, crosswalks, exception entries, attestations, tombstone), but those are attributes of a single record rather than independently registered sibling models, and contains_ids is empty. 'classifier' fits only the subordinate typology code list, not the subject. Status is accepted rather than reclassified, but the registry review_state boundary-review-required must stay open until the authority-holder cardinality rule and the per-power-type scope asymmetry recorded below are settled.

decisions.concept: Subject-model entry kind: entity versus reified relationship
decisions.rationale: The identifier persists across change of authority-holder and change of territory, which a reified holder-to-scope relationship could not do; identity independence from both endpoints is the entity test and the model enforces it explicitly.

decisions.disposition: accepted with a mandatory cardinality rule to be added
decisions.rationale: The purpose statement binds 'an identified authority-holder' (singular) while q-holder-plurality asks how several bodies sharing one scope record their distinct share. The root must be pinned as one record per holder-competence-scope tuple, with shared scope expressed through concurrency relations rather than multi-holder records.

decisions.concept: Per-power-type scope asymmetry (prescriptive reach exceeding enforcement reach)
decisions.disposition: deferred — blocking for candidate-to-accepted promotion, not for draft publication
decisions.rationale: q-power-asymmetry requires the asymmetry to be recorded rather than smoothed, but the four scope axes attach once per record, so the model's own GDPR counterexample cannot be instantiated without either scoping the axes per power type or splitting the record. The structural choice must be resolved by review before promotion.

decisions.concept: Deposited chart and coordinate-list artifact versus the no-geometry out-of-scope rule
decisions.disposition: reclassified to a citation-and-digest evidence record
decisions.rationale: media_or_form for deposited-coordinate-record lists 'nautical chart' and 'list of geographical coordinates', which reads as holding the very boundary material the out-of-scope list and the reference-over-replication policy assign to the spatial model and the depositary; only the notification reference, depositary, instant and digest should be held here.

decisions.concept: serial_naming_rule claim that AGENTS.md is the sole non-serial artifact
decisions.disposition: rejected as written; correction required before publication
decisions.rationale: Two artifacts declare serial:false — agents-bootstrap-descriptor and jurisdiction-typology-code-list — so the artifact identity rule contradicts the structure it governs. The code list is also version-governed with deprecation, so its serial flag and the rule text must be reconciled.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist assertion of eleven composition links
decisions.rationale: The frozen relationship contract is empty and the payload contains nine boundary notes and zero composition links. The ownership dimension must be restated as nine boundary notes plus named placeholder composition targets under the registry_links placeholder rule, or the count must be evidenced.

decisions.concept: Source support for State succession, cession and dissolution
decisions.disposition: accepted as declared-only; the grounding claim is struck
decisions.rationale: scope-change-succession-and-dissolution cites SRC-003, SRC-009, SRC-012 and SRC-014, none of which governs State succession; SRC-014 is the immunities convention. The lifecycle checklist note claiming succession grounding overstates the evidence and must be downgraded pending a succession instrument.

decisions.concept: urn:lex Internet-Draft as grounding for permanent identifier stability
decisions.rationale: SRC-009 is draft-spinosa-urn-lex-24, a non-consensus expiring Internet-Draft carried at authority tier 2, yet it alone carries a hard compatibility rule and a stated divergence from national code-reuse practice. The rule should also rest on ELI and ECLI persistence practice or be marked as a local policy choice.

decisions.concept: ISO 3166 held at identity tier 2 while NUTS and M49 are alignment-only
decisions.disposition: accepted with the unverified-source marker retained
decisions.rationale: The asymmetry is defensible because ISO codes are the tokens that Akoma Ntoso and urn:lex actually govern, whereas NUTS and M49 are statistical, but iso.org returned HTTP 403 so the ISO wording is unverified and every structural claim resting solely on it must stay flagged.

decisions.concept: SRC-019 (gdpr-info.eu) as a tier-3 non-primary reproduction
decisions.disposition: accepted as a non-sole supporting citation
decisions.rationale: Both findings that cite it (power-type-classification, extraterritorial-reach-and-connecting-factors) also cite SRC-016, the CELEX text, so it never carries an assertion alone; it must be marked secondary in provenance and must not become sole support in any revision.

decisions.concept: Tombstone register exemption from retention disposition
decisions.disposition: accepted with an explicit non-disposable rule required
decisions.rationale: Retention classes impose a minimum period, which read literally could authorise disposing of the append-only tombstone register and so break the identifier non-reuse guarantee and the resolution of historical ELI, ECLI and urn:lex citations; the register must be declared permanently non-disposable.

decisions.concept: Rome Statute pinned at the 1998 corrected text
decisions.disposition: accepted with a version-pin correction required
decisions.rationale: SRC-007 pins A/CONF.183/9 as adopted, which does not carry subsequently adopted amendments; the subject-matter competence catalogue and the temporal-reach claims should cite the current consolidated Statute so that catalogue versioning ties to amending instruments as q-matter-versioning demands.

decisions.concept: Missing operations for competing claims and access restrictions
decisions.disposition: deferred; no function additions permitted in single-provider mode
decisions.rationale: crud.create requires competing claims to be recorded and access.exceptions require a named approver, reason and scheduled review instant, but no declared function adds a competing claim to an existing record or registers and reviews a restriction. Raised for the next revision because add_functions must remain empty under the waiver contract.

decisions.concept: Access scopes applied to record instances
decisions.rationale: bundle, layer, finding and artifact are context-structure scopes, yet the exceptions restrict record instances and fields such as embargoed coordinate deposits and draft scope changes; a record-and-field scope must be named so instance-level restriction is expressible without stretching the context scopes.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification is outstanding: no URL, HTTP status or version pin in the nineteen-source set was re-fetched during this audit. ISO 3166-1/-2 is admittedly unretrieved (HTTP 403), SRC-009 is an expiring Internet-Draft, SRC-007 is pinned to the 1998 corrected Rome Statute text, SRC-012 to the 2024-01-01 NUTS consolidation, SRC-015 to NAL version 20260617-0, and the UNCLOS Part II and Part V URLs are legacy paths. Every pin must be revalidated with a retrieval instant and digest before the draft leaves reviewable state.

The owner-authorized absence of independent second-provider review must be visible in every published artifact: Grok was waived by the repository owner on 2026-08-29T09:06:27Z after repeated structured-output failures, so this result carries one provider plus a no-tools adversarial audit only, has no cross-provider agreement on entry kind, sources or structure, and remains a reviewable draft rather than a validated model.

The frozen registry record stays at status candidate with review_state boundary-review-required and an empty relations_ref, and the relationship contract is empty. Composition targets (spatial, legislation, case-law, entity-registry, conflict-of-laws and policy-decision/enforcement runtime models) must be published as named placeholders with intended relation types so the ownership contract is auditable before the sibling models exist.

Two artifact-identity defects must be corrected before publication: the serial_naming_rule asserts a single non-serial artifact while two are declared non-serial, and the deposited chart and coordinate-list artifact must be reduced to a citation-and-digest evidence record so it does not hold geometry the model declares out of scope.

The coverage checklist must be corrected where it overstates evidence: the claim of eleven composition links is unsupported by the frozen contract, and the State-succession grounding claim is unsupported by any cited source.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Retrieve ISO 3166-1 and ISO 3166-2 through the ISO Online Browsing Platform and re-ground every structural claim currently resting on indirect citation through Akoma Ntoso, urn:lex, UNSD and the EU Countries NAL.

Obtain a retrievable authoritative statement of the prescriptive/adjudicative/enforcement trichotomy (ILC A/61/10 annex or an equivalent doctrinal source) so power-type classification is no longer supported only by the operative structure of Brussels Ia, GDPR Article 3 and the immunities convention.

Add the HCCH 2019 Judgments Convention to the source set; recognition and refusal grounds currently rest on Brussels Ia and the 2005 Choice of Court Convention alone, which leaves recognition outside chosen-court cases unevidenced.
Consult the 1978 and 1983 Vienna Conventions on Succession of States, or an equivalent authority, to ground succession, cession and dissolution, which no cited source currently governs.

Consult the Vienna Conventions on Diplomatic Relations (1961) and Consular Relations (1963) so that privilege and immunity are not modelled solely from the 2004 State immunity convention, which is itself not universally in force.

Verify the current status of draft-spinosa-urn-lex (expiry, successor draft or RFC), the current NUTS consolidation after the triennial amendment cadence, and the current EU Countries and territories NAL version, and repin all three.

Consult UNCLOS Part XI, the Antarctic Treaty regime and the Outer Space Treaty to decide whether non-territorial competence regimes need dedicated structure or can be carried by the existing typology and functional-competence elements.

Determine whether consensual competence should be extended to arbitral seat, kompetenz-kompetenz and award enforcement by consulting the New York Convention and ICSID regime, or whether that scope belongs to a sibling model.

bundles.name: Jurisdiction Identity and Typology
bundles.description: Establishes what a jurisdiction record is, how it is uniquely and durably identified, how it aligns to external territorial code lists, and how it is classified by kind of jurisdictional entity and by type of power claimed.
bundles.rationale: Identifier stability is a normative requirement in the sources: urn:lex forbids renaming jurisdiction codes and permits only obsolescence, Akoma Ntoso requires an ISO 3166-1/-2 code in the Work IRI, and the EU Countries NAL publishes versioned governed URIs. Classification must be separated from identity because UNSD warns that grouping is a statistical convenience and implies nothing about legal status.

layers.name: Identity and Territorial Coding
layers.description: How a jurisdiction record is identified in its own right and how that identity is bound to externally governed territorial codes without absorbing their governance.

findings.name: Jurisdiction record identity and identifier stability
findings.description: The identifier for a jurisdiction record, its priority order of sources, its immutability guarantees, and how obsolescence is expressed without reuse or deletion.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is pure reference data: a small set of identifier strings, tier markers, obsolescence flags and labels that must be resolvable in any projection. Materialising it as a document would create a second master for values that are governed elsewhere and would invite drift between the artifact and the record.

findings.name: Territorial code alignment
findings.description: Assertions linking a jurisdiction to externally maintained territorial codes, each with a match strength, validity window and explicit refusal to claim conformance.

layers.name: Typology and Power Classification
layers.description: Classifies the jurisdiction by the kind of entity holding it and by the type of power asserted, keeping both as declared classifications rather than operational capabilities.

findings.name: Kind of jurisdiction
findings.description: The controlled typology of jurisdictional entities: supranational union, sovereign State, dependent or associated territory, federated or devolved sub-State unit, local authority, functional maritime zone, international tribunal, and specialised regulatory authority.

findings.name: Type of power asserted
findings.description: Records whether the jurisdiction is prescriptive, adjudicative or enforcement in nature, strictly as a declared classification with no operational capability implied.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding is a set of declared classification codes plus an explicit non-ownership pointer. Producing an artifact here would risk presenting an enforcement capability document, which belongs to the referenced policy-decision and enforcement runtime model, not to this model.

bundles.name: Authority-Holder and Conferral
bundles.description: Binds a jurisdiction to the authority that holds it, to the instrument that confers or constitutes it, and to the category and exclusivity of the competence conferred, including delegation and devolution.
bundles.rationale: TFEU Articles 2 to 6 supply a normative taxonomy of competence categories and the principle of conferral; the Rome Statute shows jurisdiction arising only where the constituting instrument's preconditions are met; ELI and Akoma Ntoso supply the identification of the instruments that must be cited rather than copied.

layers.name: Authority-Holder and Legal Basis
layers.description: Which body holds the competence and which instrument confers it, both carried by reference to their owning models.

findings.name: Authority-holder binding
findings.description: The reference to the public or legal authority that holds the competence, with role qualification and the boundary against the organisation model that masters it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The authority-holder is mastered in an external organisation or court register and is carried here strictly as a reference with a role qualifier; creating a local artifact would duplicate reference data that another model owns and would become stale on every reorganisation.

findings.name: Conferring instrument and legal basis
findings.description: Citation of the constitution, treaty, statute, delegated act or judicial instrument that creates or amends the competence, referenced through governed legal identifiers.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Instruments are owned by the legislation model identified through ELI, LEX URN and Akoma Ntoso Work IRIs. This finding therefore holds only citation tuples and relation types; producing a local instrument dossier would duplicate expression-level content and versioning that the target model governs.

layers.name: Competence Allocation and Delegation
layers.description: How competence is categorised, how exclusivity is expressed, and how it is passed downward or outward through devolution, delegation and agency.

findings.name: Competence category and exclusivity
findings.description: Whether the competence is exclusive, shared, coordinating or supporting, and what residual freedom other authorities retain when it is exercised.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Category, exclusivity and pre-emption are short coded assertions with pinpoint citations. They are consumed as structured facts by resolution queries and gain nothing from a document form, which would fragment the values across a second representation.

findings.name: Delegation, devolution and agency
findings.description: Downward or outward transfer of competence, including whether the transfer is revocable, whether the delegating authority retains oversight, and how sub-delegation is bounded.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Delegation records are relational tuples pointing at instruments held elsewhere. The instruments themselves are artifacts of the legislation or contract models; reproducing them here would create an unowned second copy with divergent version history.

bundles.name: Scope Delimitation
bundles.description: Delimits the competence along the four axes recognised across the primary sources: territorial and spatial, personal, material or subject-matter, and temporal.
bundles.rationale: The Rome Statute separates subject-matter (Art. 5), temporal (Art. 11) and territorial or nationality preconditions (Art. 12); UNCLOS fixes distinct maritime zones with different content of authority; GDPR Article 3 shows scope arising from establishment, targeting or public international law. These are independent axes and must be modelled independently.

layers.name: Territorial and Spatial Scope
layers.description: The spatial reach of the competence on land, at sea and in the air, plus reach that attaches to conduct or effects outside that space.

findings.name: Land territorial extent by reference
findings.description: Binding of the jurisdiction to administrative units and boundary features mastered in the spatial model, with the level, nesting and enclave or exclave handling.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Geometry, topology and boundary lifecycle are owned by the INSPIRE-aligned administrative-unit model. This finding holds only resolvable feature references, level codes and anomaly markers; storing an artifact would fork the authoritative geometry and break the ownership contract with the parent place model.

findings.name: Maritime, aerial and special zones
findings.description: Functional and partial competence zones seaward and skyward, where the content of authority differs by zone and rests on deposited baselines and coordinates.

findings.name: Extraterritorial reach and connecting factors
findings.description: Competence asserted over conduct, actors or effects located outside the territory, recorded with the connecting factor relied on and the known limits on giving it effect.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Extraterritorial reach is captured as coded connecting factors, indicators and limitation notes that feed resolution queries. Any document describing how such reach is actually pursued would be enforcement material owned by the referenced runtime model, so this finding stays deliberately inline.

layers.name: Personal and Material Scope
layers.description: Which persons and entities fall within the competence, and which subject matters it covers or expressly excludes.

findings.name: Personal scope and attachment
findings.description: The classes of natural and legal persons within scope and the attachment criteria that place them there, together with the priority among competing criteria.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Personal scope consists of coded class lists, ordered attachment criteria and pointers into entity registers mastered by others. It is queried as structured facts during scope resolution and would lose that queryability if flattened into a document artifact.

findings.name: Subject-matter scope
findings.description: The material competence: which matters are covered, which are expressly carved out, and how the catalogue is versioned against its instruments.

layers.name: Temporal Scope
layers.description: When the competence exists and to which conduct periods it attaches, keeping the applicability window distinct from record validity.

findings.name: Temporal applicability window
findings.description: Entry into force, start and end of applicability, non-retroactivity and any declaration that extends competence backwards, recorded separately from when the record was created or observed.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Temporal scope is a small set of instants and flags that must be directly comparable in queries at a reference instant. Any document form would obstruct the interval arithmetic that scope resolution depends on and would duplicate values the record already carries.

bundles.name: Interaction, Conflict and Exception
bundles.description: How a jurisdiction stands relative to others — hierarchy, concurrency, priority, party-chosen forum and mutual recognition — and how immunities, reservations and derogations narrow its declared scope.
bundles.rationale: Brussels Ia supplies exclusive heads, prorogation and lis pendens; the HCCH 2005 Convention supplies obligations of chosen and non-chosen courts and enumerated refusal grounds; the UN Convention on Jurisdictional Immunities supplies immunity as a default with waiver and enumerated exceptions; the Rome Statute supplies complementarity as a deference rule.

layers.name: Inter-Jurisdictional Relations
layers.description: Vertical and horizontal relations between jurisdictions and the recorded rules that break ties between them.

findings.name: Hierarchy, supremacy and deference
findings.description: Vertical ordering between jurisdictions, including which order prevails on conflict and which deference rules require a higher body to stand back where a lower one is genuinely acting.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Hierarchy is a graph of typed references between jurisdiction records with pinpoint citations. Representing it as an artifact would freeze a graph that changes whenever any participating record changes, and would duplicate edges already derivable from the records themselves.

findings.name: Concurrency, overlap and priority
findings.description: Horizontal coexistence of competences over the same matter, the classification of the overlap, and the recorded rule that assigns priority, such as first seised.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Overlap assessments are derived, instant-dependent assertions between two records. Persisting them as artifacts would present a snapshot as durable fact; they are instead recorded as dated assertions with provenance so they can be recomputed and falsified.

findings.name: Forum selection and recognition, by reference
findings.description: Party-chosen forum bindings and mutual-recognition arrangements recorded as references to their governing instruments, with the recorded grounds on which recognition may be refused.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The agreements and conventions that create forum bindings are artifacts of the contract and treaty models. This finding carries only citation references, coded refusal grounds and an explicit separation assertion, so that recognition and enforcement action stay with the models that own them.

layers.name: Exceptions and Immunities
layers.description: Overlays that narrow an otherwise applicable competence for particular beneficiaries, matters or periods.

findings.name: Immunity, privilege, reservation and derogation
findings.description: Recorded carve-outs — State immunity with its enumerated exceptions and waiver, treaty reservations and declarations, opt-outs, and time-bounded derogations — each scoped to a beneficiary class and validity window.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Provenance and Quality
bundles.description: How jurisdiction records change over time, what evidence supports them, how contested claims are held without silent resolution, and how records are validated and kept current.
bundles.rationale: Jurisdictional facts change by instrument and by succession; NUTS shows a governed amendment cadence and ELI shows versioned publication with synchronisation feeds. UNSD's caveat about legal status and the existence of competing claims require that contestation be a first-class record rather than an editorial judgement.

layers.name: Lifecycle, Succession and Cession
layers.description: State transitions of the jurisdiction record and the transfer, merger, split, suspension or termination of the competence itself.

findings.name: Scope change, succession and dissolution
findings.description: The controlled set of change events affecting a competence and the continuity links that survive a change of holder, territory or existence, including predecessor and successor bindings.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Change records are versioned state transitions on the model's own records, expressed as coded event tuples with instrument references and bitemporal instants. A durable event-log artifact would drift toward audit-trail semantics, which the boundary notes assign to the referenced runtime and to the adopting Dimension's records policy.

layers.name: Provenance, Evidence and Quality
layers.description: Where each assertion came from, how competing claims are carried without arbitration, and how records are validated and dated for currency.

findings.name: Source attestation and provenance
findings.description: Per-assertion provenance recording the official publication, the asserting party, the retrieval instant and the authority tier of the source.

findings.name: Contested claims and disputed scope
findings.description: Parallel, incompatible assertions about the same scope held side by side with their asserting authorities, without the model choosing a winner.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Contested scope must be carried as parallel, individually attributed assertions that a consumer can see in full. Materialising a single dispute dossier would invite an editorial synthesis, which is exactly the neutrality failure that the UNSD caveat warns against.

findings.name: Validation, conformance and currency
findings.description: The rule set a jurisdiction record must satisfy before publication, the refusal to claim conformance to external standards without evidence, and the freshness date attached to each record.

bundles.name: Interoperability and Operation
bundles.description: How jurisdiction records are mapped to external identifier schemes, how an agent resolves candidate jurisdictions, how the model is discovered and bootstrapped, and how access and retention are governed.
